Team / Elena — quick legal summary and asks from our side: 

1) Preferred approach (legal view): Consolidated invoicing to the US parent with a commercial appendix that maps consumption/commits by entity. This keeps Redwood's billing operations simpler and preserves single-country invoicing. To accept consolidated invoicing we need the following:
   - Tax residency evidence for the US entity to accept reverse-charge (if applicable).
   - A signed intercompany acknowledgement (we can provide a short template) stating Tessera will accept any local VAT/responsibility between its entities.

2) Net terms: Redwood can accept net45 on consolidated invoices for enterprise deals. We propose the following compromise to meet procurement needs while protecting cashflow: net45 standard + optional 1.5% discount if payment received within 30 days (applies to consolidated invoice only). For separate-entity invoicing, net30 for US / net45 for EU is acceptable but requires split minimum commit and separate SOW appendix.

3) Tax language: We will add a clause to the order form that (a) clarifies invoiced amounts will state VAT separately where applicable, and (b) requires Tessera to provide VAT registration details and certificates within 10 business days of signature to permit tax-exempt handling where eligible. If certificates are not provided, Redwood will invoice VAT in line with local compliance.

4) Invoicing triggers & minimum commit phasing: Legal is comfortable with milestone-based triggers. Please ensure MAP rows explicitly tie invoicing events to commit delivery windows (dates and usage bands). Also include an early termination proration table in appendix B to make expected credits clear across entities.

Attachment: Tax_Certificates_Request.pdf (short checklist we send to customers). I’ll upload a one-page intercompany acknowledgement template to the HubSpot deal after we choose consolidated vs separate invoicing.

If procurement prefers separate invoicing for now, we need explicit entity details and VAT IDs by EOD Fri 2026-09-10 so Sales Ops can adjust the billing schedule.

Thanks,
